newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Santos East Spar buy seen strategic.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Santos East Spar buy seen strategic.

text.p: Oil and gas producer Santos Ltd's A$181 million acquisition of WMC Ltd's 30 percent holding in the East Spar oil and gas field offshore Western Australia was welcomed on Wednesday as a good strategic move by analysts.
Most analysts contacted by Reuters were surprised by the funding mechanism, a one-for-eight rights issue, but saw it as a modest raising which would assist the company's growth.
The A$4 per share rights issue will raise about A$270 million, Santos said earlier.

One analyst, who did not want to be named, said he believed the dilutory effect of the rights issue would be around five percent, and was behind the dip early on Wednesday in the company's share price. However he said Santos had not made such a move for some time and had obviously wanted to avoid further lifting its gearing level, and he did not expect any further weakening.
"I think they may escape relatively unscathed," he said.

The analyst said the WMC acquisition was understandable, that Santos had made no secret of its desire for a larger equity stake in the Spar joint venture and was keen to develop its position in the Western Australian energy market.

Santos had obviously accelerated its pace in diversifying outside its core business in the onshore Cooper Basin, having picked up acquisitions from MIM Holdings Ltd, Parker & Parsley Petroleum Co and Cultus Petroleum NL Ltd in the past year, he said.
Another analyst said although he had not expected the rights issue, its timing was not surprising given Santos' planned A$800 spending commitment in 1997.
"It is a pretty modest raising in the overall scheme of things," he told Reuters, adding the move could be negative for Santos if investors did not see the potential benefits in the acquisition.
He believed the buy was strategic and had valued the holding at around A$200 million, with value to add through reserves and the deregulation of the Western Australian market.
"I think it will contribute positively to earnings, they may have to take a little bit of pain in the early years but I doubt it is going to be negative," he said.
"My view is the reserve base is significantly more than the contracted reserves," he said.
Another analyst was not so positive on the East Spar stake, saying he believed it would be "reasonably earnings neutral" for Santos, but he said it was a good strategic move at a fair price.
